question: The Fundamental Rights in the Indian Constitution are inspired by the ‘Bill of Rights’ of which of the following countries?
solution:
The Correct answer is__** The USA**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Fundamental Rights** enshrined in the Indian Constitution draw inspiration from the **Bill of Rights of the USA.**
 
• This segment of the American Constitution guarantees civil rights & liberties to the individual, like **freedom of speech, press, & religion,** mirroring the protections offered within the Indian Constitution.
 
• These rights form a crucial part of the democratic framework, ensuring the protection of individual liberties & serving as a check against the powers of the state.
 
• The adoption of such ideals from the** USA underscores the universal value of human rights** & democratic principles globally.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Part III** of the Indian Constitution, titled **"Fundamental Rights,"** deals with the fundamental rights guaranteed to all citizens of India.
 
• Under **Part-III, **of the constitution, every citizen has been provided with **6 fundamental rights.**
 
• A total of seven rights were originally provided by the Constitution.

 **44th Amendment 1978**, removed the **Right to property **and made a **legal right (300A).**
 
• The fundamental rights secure the natural rights of all citizens and it was taken from the **constitution of the U.S.A.**
